text:
emma: Hi team — after rotating our service-account key and switching to a signed-JWT flow we started getting 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/completions. Worked before rotation. Anyone seen this pattern?

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4521 — assigned to Support.

ben: Can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw response body? Also which exchange endpoint are you hitting (google sts / custom)?

emma: Repro steps:
```
# exchange signed JWT for access token (internal flow)
curl -X POST https://sts.example.com/token -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=$SIGNED_JWT" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
# call Redwood
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"hi"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}

ben: Thanks. Can you decode the JWT payload you used to mint the signed assertion (just the JWT you posted to sts)? Remove sensitive ids if you want, but I want to see the aud claim.

emma: Payload (redacted):
```
{
  "iss": "service-account@myproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "sub": "service-account@myproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "aud": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",
  "exp": 1700000000,
  "iat": 1699996400
}
```

carol: Ah — that's it. The signed assertion's aud is oauth2.googleapis.com which is fine for Google token exchange, but the access token returned from your STS does not contain the audience Redwood expects for API access. Our auth layer enforces that the final token's audience includes api:redwood or the host-specific audience. If you exchange against a generic oauth endpoint you can end up with a token that doesn't assert the correct aud for our gateway -> 401 invalid_api_key.

emma: I assumed the STS would mint a token scoped to the target. We use a lightweight local STS that just forwards Google's token. Is there a way to confirm the access token aud?

ben: Yes — decode the access token (if JWT) or use our introspect endpoint:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/introspect
# returns {"active":false,"error":"audience_mismatch"} or {"active":true, ...}
```

sre-oncall: On our side I pulled the ingress logs for emma's org-id. We see: `401 invalid_api_key - aud mismatch (expected: api:redwood, got: https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token)` for the failing requests. So the token the gateway saw had the wrong aud claim.

carol: Fix options:
- When minting the signed JWT for STS, set aud to the Redwood token exchange audience (e.g. `https://sts.internal.example.com/urn:redwood:exchange`) so the minted token will be accepted and the exchanged access token will contain the proper aud.
- Or skip the custom STS and use a service account flow that requests an access token with the target audience (use the target_audience parameter or Google IAM signBlob + token exchange with correct aud).
- As a short-term workaround, create a regular API key in the dashboard and use that until you can adjust the JWT aud.

emma: Thanks. I regenerated the JWT with aud set to `api:redwood` and re-ran the exchange -> introspect now returns active:true and the call to /v1/completions succeeded.

ben: Great. I'll add a note to the support docs covering STS -> Redwood aud requirements and a small troubleshooting checklist (introspect -> check aud).

carol: I'll change the error text on our gateway to include `audience_mismatch` in the response body so it's clearer next time (currently it's only in logs). Filed: ENG-1102.

emma: Appreciate the quick help :purple_heart: — marking SUP-4521 resolved on our side.
